sampling_model.design: A two-arm randomized vaccine trial is combined with an external exposure-surveillance sample from the same period-specific target environment.
sampling_model.units: For each trial arm, conditional on that arm's own realized total, the mutually exclusive categories consisting of no first infection and first infection by period and variant have the stated multinomial law. For each period-specific external total, exposure counts on \(\mathcal V_0\) have the stated multinomial law. No independence among the two trial-arm blocks and two external-period blocks is required: each block's exact error bound is first averaged over its own possibly random total, and a union bound gives simultaneous coverage unconditionally over the trial and external samples. No joint conditional coverage claim given the realized trial arm sizes is made.
sampling_model.treatment: \(A\in\{0,1\}\) has known probabilities \(\pi\), and the trial records the period and variant of each first infection.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-arm positivity is standard. Noninfecting-exposure priming is indexed by the disclosed sensitivity value \(\delta\), with \(\delta=0\) giving no priming and \(\delta=1\) permitting unrestricted priming. Fiber-wide period-two vaccine reference-risk positivity is a separate novel, LP-checkable restriction used only for finite Charnes--Cooper endpoints; the extended identified set and exact projection allow zero denominators.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The trial and exposure cell probabilities are covered by exact likelihood-ratio-ordered multinomial inversions at Bonferroni level \(\alpha/4\) for each of two arms and two periods. At total count zero, \(T_p(0)=0\) and \(\Gamma_0(0;\gamma)=\Delta\), so zero-total and zero-cell samples require no correction. For a prespecified nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\), nesting makes the sharp range set equal to \(\Theta_{I,\bar\delta}(b,q,\omega)\), where \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\); the simultaneous primitive confidence set is therefore projected through each candidate's single nonempty \(\mathcal P_{\bar\delta}(b',q',\omega)\) fiber. The resulting set covers the whole sensitivity-range identified set unconditionally and does not studentize or select an endpoint optimizer.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives sharp two-period bounds for a single-pathogen challenge effect from conventional vaccine-trial risks.
Section 4 shows that multi-variant vaccine-effectiveness measures can be time-varying under leaky and all-or-none mechanisms.
The weighted estimating-equation model permits time-varying vaccine efficacy and time-varying pathogen distributions under a marked exposure process.
Case-only strain odds ratios receive a biological relative-efficacy interpretation under stated exposure and susceptibility conditions.
Theorems 1 through 3 identify conditional relative strain efficacy from case-only data under explicit missingness and causal assumptions.
Finite latent response types and linear programming yield tight treatment-effect bounds and attaining distributions.
The paper constructs random regions with uniform asymptotic coverage of an entire identified set or its known image.
Calibrated bootstrap projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth functions of moment-constrained partially identified parameters.
Derivative-aware resampling is valid for directionally differentiable maps in settings where the ordinary bootstrap can fail.
The paper develops a powerful single-pathogen test of treatment-effect constancy and additional waning bounds.

Section 5 defines the marginal time-to-event challenge subtype effect, and the marginal-identification proposition identifies it as a ratio of two observed cause-specific hazard ratios under the paper's stated time-to-event identification and proportionality assumptions.

body.tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction. The compatible full-law classes, reduced fibers, and sharp ratio images are nested in \(\delta\); hence a nonempty closed sensitivity range \(\mathcal D\) is represented exactly by its largest value \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\), without a continuum closure. Opposite-side linear-program feasibility defines attained sharp priming breakdown points, with dual strict-sign certificates below a finite threshold and a compatible counterlaw at it. Exact multinomial inversion, including \(\Gamma_0(0;\gamma)=\Delta\), gives unconditional whole-set coverage by projecting only through the maximal fiber. The single-variant and Perényi--Stensrud anchors are projection and calibration comparisons, not class inclusions or transfers.

project_justification.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give sharp single-pathogen challenge-effect bounds, and Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) identify a variant-specific time-to-event challenge subtype effect under their own exposure and proportionality restrictions. Those results provide projection and calibration anchors, not class inclusions. Neither supplies an exact maximal-fiber sensitivity theorem, a sharp attained priming breakdown frontier, or unconditional whole-set projection for a reference-mixture ratio built from trial first-infection risks and external exposure margins when a prior noninfecting exposure may alter later controlled susceptibility.
project_justification.niche: The target compares one policy-fixed reference mixture across periods and defines period-two challenge risk after no period-one exposure. A history-indexed response array separates that target from the response after a noninfecting exposure, while \(\delta\) restricts their disagreement without substituting selected case-strain frequencies for external exposure margins. Because the restriction weakens monotonically with \(\delta\), every scientifically justified closed range \(\mathcal D\) reduces exactly to \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\); without a controlled validation substudy, \(\bar\delta=1\).
project_justification.fill: The substantive chain gives exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite reciprocal endpoints under the separate denominator condition, and common-law sign duals. It now proves law-class, fiber, and ratio-image nesting, exact equality of the sensitivity-range union with the maximal fiber, attained sharp positive- and negative-side priming breakdown points, dual certificates before each finite threshold, and compatible counterlaws at the threshold. Exact primitive-cell multinomial inversion projects through the single maximal fiber for unconditional coverage of the whole sensitivity-range identified set. For \(K=2\), the Perényi--Stensrud comparison remains a positive-face projection and calibration test, not a class-inclusion result.

body.related_work: Janvin and Stensrud (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix B) establish sharp finite single-pathogen two-period challenge-effect bounds and attaining laws. The one-variant result here is a projection and calibration check against their survivor-selection geometry; it does not assert inclusion in, or transfer to, their published class. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and the marginal \(CSE_k\) identification proposition) identify a time-to-event challenge subtype effect from observed cause-specific hazards under their stated time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, covariate-invariant exposure-ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality restrictions. Here their controlled-risk coordinates are projected onto \(\rho_{ta}(x,e^{(v)})\), and equality with their observed-hazard comparator is a calibration statement characterized by a computable quadratic cross-product on the linear-program-computed affine hull of the positive common-history face; it is not a class inclusion or transfer claim. Tomer and Biccler (2022) analyze temporal movement under specified competing-variant mechanisms. Follmann and Huang (2018), Gilbert et al. (2001), Edlefsen (2014), and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) motivate why selected infecting strains require extra exposure and susceptibility restrictions, so case frequencies are not substituted for the external margins \(q\). Balke and Pearl (1997) inform the finite response-type lift. Romano and Shaikh (2010) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) inform whole-set projection; the present exact multinomial construction includes \(\Gamma_0(0;\gamma)=\Delta\), uses a union bound without block independence, and, by sensitivity nesting, projects only through \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\) to cover the entire sensitivity-range identified set.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The parameter \(\delta\) bounds whether a period-one exposure that did not infect changes the period-two controlled response relative to no prior exposure. Routine negative tests establish noninfection, not absence of immune priming, and serial serology need not detect response-relevant cellular or mucosal changes; neither identifies a small \(\delta\). Without a randomized or controlled validation substudy, the honest range is \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\), so identification, strict-sign, and coverage audits use the unrestricted fiber at \(\bar\delta=1\). Endpoint opposite-side feasibility decides whether a sign breakdown exists, but an interior \(\delta_\star^+\) or \(\delta_\star^-\) must be located from the nested linear-program family over \([\delta_0,1]\). The finite history map still abstracts from multiple distinct noninfecting exposures within one period.
body.honest_scope: Exact common-history projection, the unconditional extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the separately disclosed fiber-wide denominator condition, and common-history sign separation hold pointwise in \(\delta\). Sensitivity nesting strengthens the range report: for every nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\), the union of compatible laws and the sharp ratio set equal their counterparts at \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\). A finite breakdown point is the attained first \(\delta\) at which the appropriate opposite-side linear program is feasible; feasibility at one only decides whether such a breakdown exists and does not locate an interior threshold. The target period-two risk uses \(R^{[0]}_{21v}\), whereas observed period-two infections use \(R^{[H_1]}_{2av}\); their discrepancy among noninfected exposees is bounded, not suppressed. The \(K=2\) and single-variant anchors are projection and calibration results only, with no claim of class inclusion or transfer to the Janvin--Stensrud or Perényi--Stensrud classes. Whole-set confidence coverage is unconditional over realized counts, uses no independence among sampling blocks, and reduces to projection through the maximal sensitivity fiber. External exposure margins remain primitives; pooled case-strain frequencies do not replace them.
